text:
After 923 games and a captaincy on Long Island, Anders Lee is a Mammoth now, playing about 14 minutes a night, and the hockey he plays hasn't changed much. He goes to the net. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.2 scoring chances per 60 from the area in front of the goal last season, 91st percentile, and a fifth of his setups came from behind the net, more than double a typical forward.

The goals haven't come yet: three on 5.8 expected, which is the clearest "due" flag on Utah's roster. With Kailer Yamamoto out, Clayton Keller has joined Lee and Barrett Hayton, and Utah takes 63% of the expected goals at five on five with Lee on the ice. That's the best case for patience. Evolving-Hockey rated him a strong play driver last season (99th percentile among forwards after adjustments), with the warning that his results ran ahead of his chances. This year it's the reverse. Our range has him around 19 goals by April; we'd trust the chances, not the current total.
